title: A Global Health Warning: Why Measles is Returning to the United States
subtitle: After years of progress, the US and other nations face a new challenge as vaccination rates fall and preventable diseases spread once again.

summary.en: The United States has officially lost its measles-free status after a significant rise in infections. Health authorities report that the virus has spread continuously for over a year, marking a major setback in public health. Experts point to declining vaccination rates and misinformation as primary causes for this resurgence. While the situation is serious, some countries like Brazil offer a model for how to fight back through rapid response and community outreach. Global health leaders warn that without higher vaccination coverage, children remain at risk of severe illness.
summary.zh: 美國在感染人數顯著上升後，已正式失去麻疹消除國的地位。衛生當局報告稱，該病毒已在境內持續傳播超過一年，這是公共衛生領域的一大挫敗。專家指出，疫苗接種率下降與錯誤資訊是導致疫情復燃的主要原因。雖然情況嚴重，但巴西等國透過快速反應與社區外展，為如何對抗疫情提供了典範。全球衛生領袖警告，若無法提高疫苗覆蓋率，兒童仍將面臨嚴重疾病的風險。

paragraphs.en: The United States has officially lost its status as a measles-free nation. This development, confirmed by the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) on November 17, 2026, marks the end of 26 years of control over the highly contagious disease. Mexico and Bolivia have also lost their measles-free status, joining a growing list of countries where the virus is spreading once again. According to The Guardian Health, nations lose this status when the same strain of the disease spreads within their borders without stopping for more than a year.
paragraphs.zh: 美國已正式失去「麻疹消除國」的地位。這項由泛美衛生組織（Pan American Health Organization, PAHO）於二〇二六年十一月十七日證實的發展，終結了該國對此類高度傳染性疾病長達二十六年的控制。墨西哥與玻利維亞也同樣失去了麻疹消除國的資格，加入全球病毒再度擴散的國家行列。根據《衛報健康版》（The Guardian Health）報導，當同一種病毒株在國境內持續傳播超過一年而未中斷時，該國即會失去此項地位。

paragraphs.en: The numbers behind this change are alarming. Deutsche Welle (DW) Top reports that the US has seen more than 5,400 cases in 2026. This is about 19 times higher than the number of cases in 2024. Most of the people who became sick were either not vaccinated or their vaccination status was unknown. Experts suggest that a sense of 'amnesia'—or forgetting how dangerous the disease can be—has contributed to this decline in protection. Because measles was rare for so long, many people stopped seeing it as a serious threat.
paragraphs.zh: 這項轉變背後的數據令人擔憂。德國之聲（Deutsche Welle, DW）報導指出，美國在二〇二六年已出現超過五千四百起病例，約為二〇二四年病例數的十九倍。大多數患者不是未接種疫苗，就是疫苗接種狀況不明。專家認為，一種「健忘症」——即遺忘了該疾病可能帶來的危險——導致了防護力下降。由於麻疹已長期罕見，許多人不再將其視為嚴重威脅。

paragraphs.en: Measles is a dangerous infection that weakens a child’s immune system. It can lead to severe health problems, including pneumonia, brain damage, hearing loss, and blindness. Dr. Eric Wobudeya, a pediatrician, described the reality of the illness in a hospital setting, noting that children often struggle to breathe as the virus attacks their lungs. According to The Guardian Health, the virus is extremely contagious; up to 90% of people who are not protected against it will catch it if they are exposed. It can stay in the air for up to two hours, making it very easy to spread in schools and other public places.
paragraphs.zh: 麻疹是一種危險的感染，會削弱兒童的免疫系統。它可能導致嚴重的健康問題，包括肺炎、腦部損傷、聽力喪失及失明。小兒科醫師艾瑞克·沃布德亞（Eric Wobudeya）在描述醫院內的真實情況時指出，當病毒攻擊肺部時，孩子們往往難以呼吸。根據《衛報健康版》報導，這種病毒傳染力極強；若未受保護，高達九成的人在接觸後會被感染。病毒可在空氣中停留長達兩小時，這使得它極易在學校及其他公共場所傳播。

paragraphs.en: Why are vaccination rates falling? Experts point to a mix of reasons, including misinformation, the disruption of health services during the COVID-19 pandemic, and a general lack of urgency. Global vaccination rates have dropped below the 95% threshold needed to create 'herd immunity'—a situation where enough people are immune to a disease that it can no longer spread easily. In 2025, only 84% of eligible children received their first dose of the measles vaccine, and that number fell to 77% for the second dose, according to The Guardian Health.
paragraphs.zh: 為什麼疫苗接種率會下降？專家指出原因錯綜複雜，包括錯誤資訊、新冠肺炎（COVID-19）疫情期間醫療服務的中斷，以及普遍缺乏急迫感。全球疫苗接種率已降至建立「群體免疫」所需的九成五門檻之下——所謂群體免疫，是指足夠多的人對疾病產生免疫力，使其無法輕易傳播。根據《衛報健康版》報導，二〇二五年僅有八成四的適齡兒童接種了第一劑麻疹疫苗，而接種第二劑的人數更降至七成七。

paragraphs.en: While the situation is difficult, some countries have shown that it is possible to regain control. Brazil, which lost its measles-free status in 2019, managed to win it back within five years. Deutsche Welle (DW) Top reports that Brazil uses a very fast response system. Health workers are required to report suspected cases within 24 hours, start an investigation within 48 hours, and vaccinate people living near the sick person within 72 hours. Brazil also uses 'Dia S' and 'Dia D' programs, where health workers visit homes, schools, and churches to find people who have not been vaccinated.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管情況嚴峻，但有些國家已證明重拾控制權是有可能的。巴西在二〇一九年失去麻疹消除國地位後，於五年內成功奪回。德國之聲報導指出，巴西採用了一套非常快速的反應系統。衛生工作者必須在二十四小時內通報疑似病例，四十八小時內啟動調查，並在七十二小時內為患者居住地周邊的人員接種疫苗。巴西還實施了「S日」與「D日」計畫，由衛生人員走訪家庭、學校與教堂，找出尚未接種疫苗的人。

paragraphs.en: Despite these efforts, the challenge remains global. PAHO Director Jarbas Barbosa noted that eliminating a disease is not a trophy that a country wins once and keeps forever; it must be protected every day. The current surge is not just a problem for the countries where cases are high. Because of international travel, an outbreak in one place can quickly move to another. Even in countries with high overall vaccination levels, there are often 'vulnerable pockets'—specific neighborhoods or communities where vaccination rates are too low to stop the virus.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管有這些努力，挑戰依然是全球性的。泛美衛生組織主任賈巴斯·巴博薩（Jarbas Barbosa）指出，消除疾病並非國家贏得一次就能永久持有的獎盃；它必須每天受到守護。目前的疫情激增不僅是高病例國家面臨的問題。由於國際旅行頻繁，一地的疫情爆發能迅速轉移至另一地。即使在整體疫苗接種率高的國家，也常存在「脆弱缺口」——即特定社區或群體，其接種率過低而無法阻擋病毒。

paragraphs.en: Looking ahead, health officials are calling for renewed focus on vaccination programs. In August 2026, the US government introduced new recommendations for children’s vaccinations in an attempt to address the falling numbers. However, experts warn that the world is losing ground against a disease that is entirely preventable. With nearly 59 million lives saved by the measles vaccine since 2000, advocates like Catherine Russell of Unicef emphasize that we must not allow this progress to disappear. Protecting children from measles requires constant effort, clear communication, and a commitment to reaching every child with the vaccine.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，衛生官員呼籲重新聚焦於疫苗接種計畫。二〇二六年八月，美國政府針對兒童疫苗接種提出了新建議，試圖解決數據下滑的問題。然而，專家警告，人類正在對一種完全可預防的疾病節節敗退。自二〇〇〇年以來，麻疹疫苗已挽救了近五千九百萬人的生命，聯合國兒童基金會（Unicef）的凱瑟琳·羅素（Catherine Russell）等倡議者強調，我們絕不能讓這些進展消失。保護兒童免受麻疹侵害，需要持續的努力、清晰的溝通，以及確保每一位兒童都能接種疫苗的承諾。

keyTerms.definitionEn: The power to influence or direct people's behavior or the course of events.
keyTerms.noteZh: 此處指對疾病傳播的抑制能力，而非單純的「控制」動作。文中：marks the end of 26 years of control over the highly contagious disease.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To become less successful or to be in a weaker position than before.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 處於劣勢、節節敗退、失去優勢。
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面上是「失去土地」，實際指在對抗疾病的過程中處於不利地位。文中：However, experts warn that the world is losing ground against a disease that is entirely preventable.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Small, isolated areas or groups that are different from the surrounding area.
keyTerms.definitionZh: （特定區域的）小群體、局部地區。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（口袋），這裡指地理上分散的小區域。文中：Even in countries with high overall vaccination levels, there are often 'vulnerable pockets'—specific neighborhoods or communities where vaccination rates are too low to stop the virus.

quiz.question: According to the article, what is the specific requirement for a country to officially lose its 'measles-free' status?

options.A: It must have more than 5,000 cases reported within a single calendar year.
options.B: A single strain of the virus must circulate continuously within its borders for over 12 months.
options.C: Its national vaccination rate must drop below the 77% threshold for two consecutive years.
options.D: The Pan American Health Organization must confirm that the disease has spread to more than three neighboring countries.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據第一段最後一句，國家失去無麻疹狀態的條件是「同一種病毒株在境內持續傳播超過一年」。選項 A 雖提到 5,400 例，但這是 2026 年的數據，並非失去地位的定義。選項 C 提到的 77% 是疫苗接種率數據，而非失去地位的標準。選項 D 為錯誤資訊，文中並未提及鄰國數量與失去地位的關聯。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the 'vulnerable pockets' mentioned in the sixth paragraph?

options.A: They are areas where the local population has developed a natural immunity to the measles virus.
options.B: They are geographic regions that have been completely isolated from international travel.
options.C: They are communities where the risk of an outbreak remains high despite national vaccination averages.
options.D: They are neighborhoods that have successfully implemented the 'Dia S' and 'Dia D' vaccination programs.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。第六段提到即便整體接種率高的國家，仍有這些「脆弱區域」，這暗示了即使國家平均數據好看，局部地區因接種率過低，仍可能成為病毒爆發的溫床。選項 A 與文意相反，脆弱區域正是因為缺乏免疫力。選項 B 與國際旅遊導致疾病傳播的論點矛盾。選項 D 錯誤，這些區域正是因為缺乏有效接種才被稱為脆弱。

quiz.question: In the second paragraph, the author uses the word 'amnesia' to describe the public's attitude toward measles. What does this suggest?

options.A: People have forgotten the severity and danger of the disease due to its long-term absence.
options.B: The public is suffering from a medical condition that causes memory loss regarding health records.
options.C: Parents are intentionally choosing to ignore the vaccination advice provided by pediatricians.
options.D: The government has failed to keep accurate records of past measles outbreaks.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。文中將 'amnesia'（失憶症）用於描述大眾對麻疹的態度，這是一種隱喻，表示因為麻疹長期罕見，人們忘記了它曾經造成的威脅。選項 B 將隱喻誤解為生理疾病。選項 C 雖提到家長行為，但 'amnesia' 強調的是「遺忘」而非「蓄意忽視」。選項 D 錯誤，文中並未指責政府紀錄缺失。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article regarding the current measles situation?

options.A: The COVID-19 pandemic is the sole reason for the global decline in childhood vaccination rates.
options.B: Brazil’s response system is the only effective way for nations to regain their measles-free status.
options.C: Measles is a minor illness that has become a political issue rather than a public health concern.
options.D: Maintaining measles-free status requires constant vigilance and a renewed commitment to global vaccination efforts.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。文章整體論述了麻疹回歸的現狀、原因以及應對方式，並引述專家觀點強調消除疾病非一勞永逸，必須持續努力。選項 A 將原因簡化為單一因素（文中還有誤導資訊與缺乏急迫感等因素）。選項 B 錯誤，巴西模式僅是範例，並非唯一方法。選項 C 與文章強調麻疹會導致肺炎、腦損傷等嚴重後果的描述完全相反。
